title: Scruple — rational creature’s assent should not outrun its grounds
source_text: XXXI. Verum ista sic nude & breviter proposita scrupulum aliquem in animo relinquunt. Sicut enim non congruit creaturae rationali, ut ulli rei assensum praebeat, quin ante ipsa per se veritatem ejus percipiat, vel ex quibusdam signis & argumentis colligat, aut saltem ad credendum moveatur gravi quadam authoritate: Ita quoque eidem congruere non videtur, ut certior sit ejus assensus quam possunt argumenta quibus movetur ad assentiendum. Alioquin in isto assensu erit saltem gradus aliquis ratione omni destitutus, ac nulli solido fundamento subnixus, quod abhorret a genio creaturae rationalis. Constituendum est autem Spiritum Sanctum fidem aliasque virtutes, sive virtutum actus in nobis operari modo quodam naturae congruo & consentaneo, & qui licet sit supra naturam, minime tamen est naturae contrarius.
pass_a_gloss: But these things so nakedly and briefly proposed leave some scruple in the mind. For just as it does not befit a rational creature to afford assent to any thing before it either perceives its truth through itself, or gathers it from certain signs and arguments, or at least is moved to believe by some grave authority: so also it does not seem to befit the same that its assent be more certain than the arguments by which it is moved to assent can bear. Otherwise in that assent there will be at least some grade destitute of all reason and resting on no solid foundation, which abhors the genius of a rational creature. But it is to be laid down that the Holy Spirit works faith and the other virtues, or acts of virtues, in us in a manner somehow congruent and consentaneous with nature, and which though it be above nature is yet by no means contrary to nature.
pass_b_english: Naked Spirit-imprint story leaves a scruple.
Rational assent shouldn’t outrun its grounds (perception/signs/authority).
Else a reason-less grade — against rational creature’s genius.
Spirit works above nature, not against it.
